summary: We developed SOL ZERO, a free 2D browser game in which students play a research astronaut sent to Mars. The problem we address is that students usually learn Mars as a list of facts to memorise, without feeling why a real mission depends on careful planning. Our solution turns those facts into decisions with consequences: players explore, collect samples and report to Earth, while balancing oxygen, water, food, health and energy, sheltering from solar radiation waves, closing ceramic shields over their crops and repairing an engine broken by dust storms. Mistakes teach instead of ending the game, and 25 guided quests explain every mechanic. The environment is based on NASA data. The project matters because it makes space science active, memorable and free for any classroom. It is aimed at middle and high school students and teachers, runs on school computers and phones without installation, and is playable in four languages.
details:
What it does: SOL ZERO is a 2D browser game in which students play a research astronaut on Mars. They explore, collect metal and rare rock samples, send rocks to Earth for analysis and report findings, while keeping oxygen, water, food, health and energy in balance until the flight home.

How it works: Each frame the game reads keyboard, mouse or touch input, updates survival values, farming, weather, radiation and quests, then redraws the world. Every 3 sols a radiation wave hits: players shelter in the rocket and close ceramic crop shields with Q. Dust storms break the engine, which is repaired step by step. At zero health the astronaut wakes in the sleep pod.

Problem: Students learn Mars as a list of facts. SOL ZERO turns those facts into decisions with consequences.

Benefits: It is free, needs no installation or account, runs on school computers and phones, works offline once loaded and is playable in four languages. 25 guided quests make it usable in class.

Goal: Students understand why a Mars mission depends on planning: protect resources, check before acting, repair systems.

Technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas 2D, WebGL (menu), Web Audio, localStorage; Visual Studio Code, Prettier, Playwright; NASA JPL and Curiosity RAD data. Built with Anthropic’s AI assistant Claude under our team’s direction. No hardware needed.
